title: SettingsPage
wrapsNative: MonarchListRow rows that push a detail screen, androidx.activity.compose.BackHandler, MonarchSectionCard, MonarchFormActionsBar and MonarchUnsavedChangesGuard; androidx.compose.material3.adaptive.navigation.NavigableListDetailPaneScaffold on wide windows
summary: A recipe, not a component: a settings screen as a list of sections, each opening its own detail screen with its settings, a save bar while there are unsaved changes, a guard before leaving them, and the danger zone last.
whenToUse: An app or workspace has several groups of settings (profile, notifications, billing, members) that people change from time to time.
whenNotToUse: For one short group of settings, show a single settings-section recipe on the screen. For settings that save as soon as they change, use MonarchSwitchSettingsList without a save bar.
api: MonarchListRow(headlineContent = { Text("Notifications") }, supportingContent = { … }, onClick = { section = "notifications" }, divider = true)
MonarchUnsavedChangesGuard(hasChanges = dirty, open = asking, onOpenChange = …, onLeave = { section = null }, onSave = …)

options.name: sections
options.description: One row per group of settings, with a short summary as supporting text; the danger zone row comes last.

options.name: section
options.description: The open section, kept in rememberSaveable (or the app's navigation); null shows the list.

options.name: dirty
options.description: Whether the open section's draft differs from what is saved: shows the save bar and turns on the guard.

options.name: onSave
options.description: Saves the open section, from the save bar and from Save in the guard.

options.name: onDiscard
options.description: Puts the draft back to what is saved.

states.name: list
states.description: The title and one row per section; each row opens its detail screen.

states.name: detail
states.description: The section's settings in a MonarchSectionCard, with a back button and system back to the list.

states.name: unsaved changes
states.description: MonarchFormActionsBar shows Save and Discard; back or the back button opens MonarchUnsavedChangesGuard.

states.name: danger zone
states.description: The last row opens the danger-zone recipe: a danger-toned card with its confirmed actions.

states.name: wide window
states.description: On a tablet or a desktop window NavigableListDetailPaneScaffold shows the list and the open section side by side.

appearance: List rows on the surface color separated by subtle dividers, the danger row's title in the strong danger text color; detail screens use MonarchSectionCard, the save bar and the guard dialog. Every part is an existing component, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web ships SettingsPage: a title, a section navigation (a sticky side list, a scrolling strip on phones), all sections on one long page, a page-wide save bar and a guard on leaving. Android follows the system Settings pattern instead: the screen is a list of sections and each opens its own detail screen, which saves on its own; system back returns to the list. That is why there is no Android component: the list rows, BackHandler, MonarchSectionCard, MonarchFormActionsBar and MonarchUnsavedChangesGuard already cover it, and the app's own navigation (or NavigableListDetailPaneScaffold from the split-layout entry on wide windows) holds the open section. The web's interceptLinks, guardRef and activeSection have no Android equivalent: components do not navigate.
accessibility: Each section row is one TalkBack element with the Button role, its title and summary read together, and a target of at least 48dp from MonarchListRow.
The danger zone is named by its title, not by color alone.
System back returns to the list, and while there are unsaved changes MonarchUnsavedChangesGuard asks first.
The save bar announces unsaved changes and keeps Save and Discard as 48dp buttons, from MonarchFormActionsBar.
edgeCases: Keep each row's summary to one line, such as the current value; long summaries wrap.
Save per section: a change in one section never waits for another.
When the app uses its own navigation library, replace the section state with its back stack and keep the guard on each detail screen.
